questionText: Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE while computing $First$ and $Follow$ during top down parsing by a compiler?
options: For a production $A \rightarrow \epsilon$, $\epsilon$ will be added to $First(A)$.
If there is any input right end marker, it will be added to $First(S)$, where $S$ is the start symbol.
For a production $A \rightarrow \epsilon$, $\epsilon$ will be added to $Follow(A)$.
If there is any input right end marker, it will be added to $Follow(S)$, where $S$ is the start symbol.
explanation:
Step 1: Rules for computing $First$ sets
• If $X$ is a terminal, then $First(X) = \{X\}$.
• If $X \rightarrow \epsilon$ is a production, then add $\epsilon$ to $First(X)$. Hence, Statement (A) is TRUE.
• If $X$ is a non-terminal and $X \rightarrow Y_1 Y_2 \dots Y_k$, then add $First(Y_1 Y_2 \dots Y_k)$ to $First(X)$.

Step 2: Rules for computing $Follow$ sets
• Place $\$ $ (the input right end-marker) in $Follow(S)$, where $S$ is the start symbol. Hence, Statement (D) is TRUE.
• $\epsilon$ (epsilon) is NEVER placed in any $Follow$ set. $Follow$ sets contain only terminals and the end-marker $\$$. Therefore, Statement (C) is FALSE.
• $First$ sets contain terminals and $\epsilon$, but not the end-marker $\$$. Therefore, Statement (B) is FALSE.

Thus, statements (A) and (D) are correct.
